subject.title: Preserve structured ACP backend error kinds instead of mapping all errors to `end_turn`

question: Should non-refusal ACP backend failures reject `session/prompt` with structured `RequestError`, keep resolving `PromptResponse` while exposing structured failure data elsewhere, or use another approved ACP-compatible surface?
rationale: The current bridge can see Gateway error kinds, but changing ACP prompt settlement is client-visible compatibility behavior that code inspection cannot safely choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Settle the contract in the linked PR
options.body: Approve a specific ACP prompt failure representation, require non-conflicting error codes/data, and land the linked PR or replacement with tests and real ACP proof.

options.title: Preserve resolved prompt responses
options.body: Keep existing `PromptResponse` settlement as the default and expose structured failure data through an approved metadata, diagnostic, or event surface.

options.title: Pause for a maintainer replacement
options.body: Leave this issue open and ask for a narrower maintainer-led implementation if the current PR cannot settle the compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Settle the contract in the linked PR
recommendation.body: Approve a specific ACP prompt failure representation, require non-conflicting error codes/data, and land the linked PR or replacement with tests and real ACP proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current structured error-kind implementation and focused ACP tests trace to `steipete`, making this the strongest routing signal for the contract decision.
